properties.headline: Fire Warning issued September 15 at 1:20PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
FRWOUN

The National Weather Service in Norman has issued a
Fire Warning at the request of Oklahoma Forestry Services for
southwestern Canadian and northeastern Caddo Counties until at least
315 PM CDT.

* AT 118 PM CDT, a dangerous wildfire was located 6 miles east of
Binger, moving rapidly north at 2 mph.

* Areas impacted....Areas near and south of Scott and south of Niles.

* Additional Information...Smoke and fire will present a threat to
life and property.
properties.instruction:
Be prepared to evacuate quickly if requested and follow all safety
instructions from local emergency management officials. Do not drive
into smoke.

Firefighters and incident responders should anticipate extreme fire
behavior including wind-driven runs, torching, and spot fires.
Dangerous fire behavior may exceed traditional offensive suppression
tactics and require immediate actions to protect life and property.

properties.description:

miles north of Big Water, or 38 miles south of Escalante, moving
northeast at 20 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts of 50 to 55 mph and nickel size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around

County.

localized flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

FFWGJT

The National Weather Service in Grand Junction has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Babylon burn scar in...
Central San Juan County in southeastern Utah...

* Until 100 PM MDT.

* At 958 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Babylon Burn Scar. Flash flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar
will result in debris flow. The debris flow can consist of rock,
mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Babylon Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Babylon Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Central San Juan County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Babylon Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 15 at 7:31AM AKDT until September 15 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by onshore flow restricting Kuskokwim River
drainage in combination with excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim near Bethel.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of water in areas is
occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 715 AM AKDT, river gauges in Bethel have detected a rise in
water level above 8.5 feet. River gauge reports indicate rises in
water levels from the Kuskokwim River back-up in combination with
heavy rain across the advisory area. This is causing minor
flooding from overflow of poor drainage areas, especially along
the Kuskokwim.
- Strong onshore winds along the Kuskokwim coast have limited the
ability for the Kuskokwim River to drain out into the Bering Sea.
This has caused rapid river rises along the coast and inland into
Bethel. Water levels are expected to back up along Brown Slough
and flood low lying areas of Bethel and areas along the
Kuskokwim.
- For Kuskokwim River at Bethel:
At 6:50am the stage was 8.6 feet.
Flood Stage is 8.5 feet.

Impacts:
At 7.0 feet: Action and bankfull stage.
At 8.5 feet: Minor flood stage. Water starts to back up along Brown
Slough and flood low lying areas.
At 12.0 feet: Moderate flood stage.
At 14.0 feet: Major flood stage.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

If you live near or along the Kuskokwim River stay alert and be
prepared to take action.

morning before slowly diminishing Wednesday afternoon.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 14 at 3:36PM AKDT until September 18 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Upper Kuskokwim Valley. This
includes the cities of McGrath, Nikolai, And Takotna.

* WHEN...Through Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...The Kuskokwim River is currently at bankfull. Soils
remain moist and excessive runoff may result in localized flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rain is forecasted to begin Monday afternoon. Rain should
continue through Wednesday morning with storm total rainfall
expected to be around 1 to 2 inches. Minor pooling/ponding of
water in low-lying and flood prone areas is possible with the
already saturated ground conditions beginning on Tuesday. Small
stream and creek flooding is possible as we expect very high
water levels throughout the week in response to the heavy rain.

- The Kuskokwim River dropped below bankfull Monday morning.
River levels are expected to rise again in response to the heavy
rain beginning Monday afternoon and remain high through the rest
of the week.

- We will continue to monitor the situation closely and update as
necessary.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared to take
action should flooding develop.

Soils remain moist and excessive runoff may result in flooding of
rivers, creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone
locations.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. More rain is expected beginning
Tuesday and will continue through Wednesday afternoon. Storm
total rainfall during this time will be around 0.50" to 1.00". It
has been very wet lately and this amount of rain has the
potential to bring the Chena and Little Chena Rivers above minor
flood stage beginning Wednesday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding from Wednesday through the end of
the week as water levels gradually rise then fall. In addition,
while we are not expecting much flooding away from rivers,
streams and creeks, as the ground is already saturated and may
struggle to hold more water. This can lead to pooling and ponding
of water across the area which may make travel difficult in
localized spots.

- There is some uncertainty with exact timing and amounts of
rainfall but as details become clearer, we will continue to
update.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc

- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 14 at 3:13PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Willow and Talkeetna
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains

Timing:

* This (Monday) evening through Wednesday afternoon. Heaviest
rainfall expected late Tuesday morning through Tuesday night.

Rainfall:

* Rainfall totals of 1 to 3 inches Monday through Wednesday likely
won't be high enough for widespread flooding, but smaller
tributaries draining the Talkeetnas including Willow Creek and the
Little Susitna may reach bankfull.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.
